corpusOverrides.note: All four started from the Japanese file. 疐 → MM, 冢 → MM and 褫 → Hans came out clean, because Ja writes the inner vertical of 叀 before the bar, reorders the legs of 豕, and writes the long left sweep of 虍 before the bar above it. 摧 → MM dropped three flagged strokes to one; the stroke left over is the top-right tick of 隹 and was redrawn.

directionProbe.threshold: angle over 60° between dictionary and candidate start-to-end vectors
directionProbe.note: 疐, 冢 and 褫 disappeared when the corpus changed, and 摧 shrank from three to one. 嚔, 嘬, 騅 and 疃 were resolved by reordering and 譙, 摧, 鶖, 騅 and 瘳 by an authored path. The endpoint assignment check added 惙, 啜 and 掇, whose 叕 strokes run in the same directions and differ only in order. Recomputed against the published order and paths, no stroke is over 60°.

endpointOnlyFindings.note: 叕 is four 又 in a two by two grid. The dictionary writes the left column top to bottom and then the right column; all five corpora write the top row and then the bottom row. Every stroke runs the same way, so the angle probe reads nothing; the assignment check separates them by hundreds. The same difference appeared in all three glyphs that carry 叕.

subThresholdSlants.method: direction-probe rows recomputed against the published order and paths: 12 rows between 45° and 60°, none corrected
subThresholdSlants.note: Short opening dots and marks the dictionary draws vertically or steeper than the licensed corpora (彘 2 at 47°, 甃 6 at 60°, 蹜 8 at 54°, 瘁 1 at 56° and 6 at 46°, 廁 1 at 49°, 褫 1 at 46°, 庤 1 at 56°, 佗 3 at 49°, 沱 4 at 55°, 它 1 at 53°, 疃 6 at 56°). Kept as licensed geometry, as in the earlier batches. 甃 6 at exactly 60° is the closest a kept stroke has come to the threshold.

sourceTransform.note: No dictionary group in this batch carries a horizontal offset; every transform is translate(0, -y). The first batch since batch 4 with none.
